label: Slope size
compute: // Slope after Skitourenguru's Relevant Slope Area: bounded by the next terrain fold
// (ridge, gully bottom, slope edge, toe; fold = angle between neighbouring slope normals)
// or where the terrain flattens below the minimum angle. Follow the fall line up and down
// from the skier and report the height between the top and the bottom of that slope.
// 1. Find the slope: right here, or within u_below metres uphill (skier below the toe).
g = vec2(elev(p + vec2(h, 0.0)) - elev(p - vec2(h, 0.0)), elev(p + vec2(0.0, h)) - elev(p - vec2(0.0, h))) / (2.0 * h);
// 2. Up the fall line until it flattens or crosses a fold.
vec2 gn = vec2(elev(qn + vec2(h, 0.0)) - elev(qn - vec2(h, 0.0)), elev(qn + vec2(0.0, h)) - elev(qn - vec2(0.0, h))) / (2.0 * h);
if (length(gn) < tanMin || dot(nn, nq) < cosFold) break;
q = qn; gq = gn; nq = nn;
// 3. Down the fall line from the same start until it flattens or crosses a fold.
vec2 gn = vec2(elev(qn + vec2(h, 0.0)) - elev(qn - vec2(h, 0.0)), elev(qn + vec2(0.0, h)) - elev(qn - vec2(0.0, h))) / (2.0 * h);
if (length(gn) < tanMin || dot(nn, nq) < cosFold) break;
q = qn; gq = gn; nq = nn;
// Full colour inside the slope, paler the further below its toe.

presentation.footnote: Height from bottom to top of the slope, bounded by terrain folds or flattening (after Skitourenguru). Bands: <60, 60–100, 100–200, 200–300, >300 m. Paler colour: below the slope's toe. No forest data.
